Rashi on Ketubot 25a:10:1.english: In bei rav - The study hall is called bei rav.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:10:2.hebrew: נתחייבו בחלה - דכתיב "בבואכם אל הארץ", ותניא בספרי: ר' ישמעאל אומר, שינה הכתוב ביאה זו מכל ביאות שבתורה, שבכולן נאמר "כי תבאו", "כי יביאך", וכאן "בבואכם", ללמדך שכיון שנכנסו לה, נתחייבו:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:10:2.english: They were obligated in ḥalla - As it is written: "When you come into the land," and it is taught in Sifrei: Rabbi Yishmael says: Scripture varied this [expression of] coming from all [other] comings in the Torah; for in all of them it is stated "when you come" [ki tavo'u] [or] "when He brings you" [ki yevi'akha], whereas here [it states] "upon your coming" [bevo'akhem], to teach you that as soon as they entered it, they became obligated.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:10:3.hebrew: ולא נתחייבו בתרומות ומעשרות - דכתיב "דגנך", "תבואת זרעך" — המיוחדת לך. ועוד, שהרי תלה הכתוב המעשר במנין שנות השמטה, דכתיב "בשנה השלישית שנת המעשר", ושמטות לא מנו אלא משכבשו וחילקו, כדאמרינן בסדר עולם ובמסכת ערכין (דף יב:):
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:10:3.english: And they were not obligated in terumot and tithes - For it is written: "your grain" [and] "the yield of your seed" — [meaning] that which is uniquely yours. And furthermore, Scripture made the tithe dependent on the count of the Sabbatical years, as it is written: "in the third year, the year of the tithe," and they did not count Sabbatical [years] until after they had conquered and divided [the land], as we say in Seder Olam and in Tractate Arakhin (12b).

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:11:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן: אי "בבואכם", יכול משנכנסו לה שנים ושלשה מרגלים, תלמוד לומר "בבואכם" — בביאת כולכם כו' - והכי פירושו: כיון דשינה הכתוב ביאה זו לכתוב בה "בבואכם" ולא כתב "כי תבאו", יכול משנכנסו לה מרגלים? ת"ל כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:11:1.english: This is the reading: If "When you come" [בבואכם], [one] might [think that it took effect] once two or three spies entered it; the verse states "When you come" [בבואכם] — with the coming of all of you, etc. - And this is its explanation: Since Scripture varied [the phrasing of] this entry to write in it "When you come" [בבואכם], and did not write "When you come" [כי תבאו], could it be [that the obligation began] once spies entered it? [Therefore] the verse states ["When you come"], etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:1:1.hebrew: ואלא מאי גדולה חזקה - דקאמר ר' יוסי, למה לנו [לחוש] להשבית חזקתם, כי מה יש לחוש לבטלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:1:1.english: And what, then, [is] "great is presumptive status" - that Rabbi Yose said — why should we [be concerned] to suspend their presumptive status, for what is there to be concerned about to nullify it?

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:1:2.hebrew: בתרומה דרבנן - שהרי בגולה היו, שאין שם תרומה מן התורה, דכל מצוה שהיא תלויה בארץ אינה נוהגת אלא בארץ, כדאמרינן בקידושין (דף לו:):
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:1:2.english: Of teruma by rabbinic [law] - For they were in the exile, where there is no teruma by Torah [law], as every mitzva that is dependent on the Land [of Israel] applies only in the Land [of Israel], as we say in Kiddushin (36b).

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:2:1.english: And if you wish, say: Now too, they partake of terumah by rabbinic [law] - Terumah of tree fruits and vegetables.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:2:2.hebrew: דאורייתא - דגן, תירוש ויצהר לא אכול, ומש"ה לא קשיא למ"ד מעלין מתרומה ליוחסין, דכי מסקינן ליוחסין, מתרומה דאורייתא כו':
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:2:2.english: By Torah law - [Namely,] grain, wine, and oil they did not eat, and therefore it is not difficult according to the one who says we elevate from teruma to [priestly] lineage, for when we elevate to [priestly] lineage, [it is] from teruma [obligated] by Torah law, etc.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:2:3.hebrew: דאיכא למיגזר משום תרומה דאורייתא - שהרי לארץ באו, ומצויה שם תרומה גמורה דאורייתא, מה שלא היה מצוי להם בגולה, ויש לחוש פן יאכילום בה:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:2:3.english: That there is [reason] to issue a decree due to teruma by Torah law - For behold, they have come to the Land [of Israel], and full teruma by Torah law is common there — which was not common for them in the Diaspora — and there is [reason] to be concerned lest they feed them of it.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:4:1.english: Not of something that is called kodesh - And this is teruma.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:4:2.hebrew: וכל זר לא יאכל קדש - בתרומה משתעי, דכתיב בפרשה לעיל מיניה: "ובא השמש וטהר ואחר יאכל מן הקדשים", ואוקמינן בתרומה ביבמות בהערל (יבמות דף עד:):
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:4:2.english: And no non-priest shall eat of the holy thing - It speaks of terumah, as it is written in the passage above it: “And when the sun sets, he shall be pure, and afterward he may eat of the holy things,” and we established [it as referring] to terumah in Yevamot, in [the chapter] He’arel (Yevamot 74b).

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:4:3.english: Nor of anything that is called kodashim - Even the breast and thigh of peace-offerings, which are eaten by the wives of priests and by their slaves.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:4:4.hebrew: ואמר מר - ביבמות בפרק יש מותרות, בבת כהן שניסת לישראל ונעשית אלמנה וגרושה וזרע אין לה, שחוזרת לתרומת אביה ואינה חוזרת לחזה ושוק. ויליף לה מהאי קרא: כי תהיה לאיש זר, היא בתרומת הקדשים לא תאכל עוד:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:4:4.english: And the Master said - In Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Mutarot, [it is taught] regarding a priest’s daughter who married an Israelite [i.e., a non-priest] and became a widow or a divorcée and has no offspring, that she returns to [eating] her father’s terumah, but does not return to [eating] the breast and the thigh [of offerings]. And [the Gemara there] derives it from this verse: “[When] she is married to a common man, she shall not eat of the terumah of the holy things” anymore:

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:1.english: Presumptive status for priesthood - To testify about him that he is a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:2.hebrew: נשיאות כפים בבבל - הרואהו נושא כפיו בבבל, מעיד עליו בכל מקום שהוא כהן ומקבלין הימנו, לפי שיש שם ישיבה וב"ד קבוע, בודקין אחר נושאי כפים. אבל אכילת חלה ותרומה אינה חזקה, דחוצה לארץ לאו דאורייתא תרומה דיליה, ולא קפדי כולי האי:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:2.english: The lifting of hands in Babylonia - One who sees him lifting his hands in Babylonia may testify about him anywhere that he is a priest, and they accept [his testimony] from him, because there is an academy and an established court there, [and] they investigate those who lift their hands. However, partaking of ḥalla and teruma is not a presumptive status, for outside the Land [of Israel], its teruma is not [required] by Torah law, and they are not so strict [about it].

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:3.hebrew: ואכילת חלה בסוריא - היא ארם צובה שכיבשה דוד וחיברה לא"י, וקסבר האי תנא כיבוש יחיד שמיה כיבוש, וחלתה ותרומתה דאורייתא. וקס"ד תנא חלה, וה"ה לתרומה:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:3.english: And partaking of challah in Syria - This is Aram Tzovah, which David conquered and annexed to the Land of Israel; and this Tanna holds that a conquest by an individual is considered a [valid] conquest, and its challah and its terumah are [obligatory] by Torah law. And we initially assumed [that the baraita] taught challah, and the same applies to terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:4.english: And distributing gifts - Of the foreleg and the jaws.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:5.hebrew: בכרכין - ואע"ג דאיסורן אין איסור לזרים, הואיל וכרכים מקום שווקין הן ומצויין בו עוברים ושבים המכירין בו, אי לאו דכהן הוה לא מחציף נפשיה:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:5.english: In the cities - And even though their prohibition is not a prohibition for non-priests [to eat them], since cities are places of markets and passersby who recognize him are frequent there, if he were not a priest, he would not act so brazenly.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:6.hebrew: לא לתרומה - הרואהו נושא כפיו בבבל, או אוכל חלה דווקא בסוריא, והעיד עליו בא"י, מקבלין עדותו להאכילו תרומה, אבל לא ליוחסין:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:5:6.english: No, for terumah - One who sees him lifting his hands in Babylonia, or eating challah specifically in Syria, and testifies about him in the Land of Israel — we accept his testimony to feed him terumah, but not for [establishing] lineage.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:6:1.english: Just as partaking of challah - [the] testimony of its presumptive status [is for lineage].

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:6:2.hebrew: ליוחסין - דאי לתרומה, פשיטא; היא גופה תרומה היא וכבר הוחזק בה:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:6:2.english: For lineage - For if [it were] for terumah, [that is] obvious — [challah] itself is terumah and he has already established presumptive status regarding it.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:6:3.hebrew: ומסקינן מחלה דרבנן כו' - דאי לאו כהן הוא, לא הוו ספו ליה חלה, גזירה משום תרומה:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:6:3.english: And we elevate from challah [which is] by rabbinic [law], etc. - For if he were not a priest, they would not have fed him challah, [as] a decree on account of terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:6:4.english: And as [Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua] reversed - [The Gemara] explains [this] below.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:1.english: Lifting of hands and distribution [at] the threshing floors - Of terumah.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:2.hebrew: בא"י - נושאי כפים, דאיכא ב"ד קבועין ובדקי. וחילוק גרנות, קס"ד השתא דתרומה בזמן הזה דאורייתא, וכיון דעון מיתה איכא, מסקינן מינה ליוחסין:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:2.english: In Eretz Yisrael - Lifting of hands [constitutes proof], because there are established courts and they investigate. And [regarding] distribution [at] the threshing floors, we currently assume that teruma nowadays is by Torah law; and since there is a sin [punishable by] death [involved], we elevate [one] from it to [confirmed] lineage.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:3.hebrew: בסוריא וכ"מ ששלוחי א"י מגיעין - להודיע לגולה יום שקידשו ב"ד את החדש לעשות פסח בזמנו, דהיינו היושבים בתוך מהלך חמשה עשר יום:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:3.english: In Syria and every place that the emissaries of the Land of Israel arrive - [that is,] to inform the Diaspora of the day on which the court sanctified the New Moon, so as to observe Passover in its proper time — namely, those residing within a fifteen-day journey.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:4.hebrew: נשיאות כפים ראיה - לפי שב"ד קבוע שם, שמקבל שליחות החדש של ב"ד הגדול:
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:4.english: The lifting of hands [is] proof - Because a court is established there that receives the mission of the New Moon from the Great Court.

Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:5.hebrew: אבל לא חילוק גרנות - דתרומה דידהו לאו דאורייתא, ובסוריא נמי האי תנא סבר כיבוש יחיד לא שמיה כיבוש, ופלוגתא דתנאי היא בהך מילתא (ע"ז דף כא.):
Rashi on Ketubot 25a:7:5.english: But not distribution [at the] threshing floors - Because their terumah is not [obligatory] by Torah law; and in Syria as well, this Tanna holds [that] an individual's conquest is not considered a conquest, and it is a dispute of Tannaim regarding this matter (Avodah Zarah 21a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:1:1.hebrew: ואלא מאי גדולה חזקה - בשלמא אי אין מעלין, ניחא הא דגדולה חזקה, אע"ג דאיכא למיחש לב"ד טועין שיעלו מן נשיאות כפים לקדשי קדשים [ואע"ג דבלא חזקה מעלין לתרומה ע"פ עד אחד, ולא חיישינן לב"ד טועין שמא יעלו ליוחסין — השתא סבר המקשן דיוחסין חמירא ולא אתו למיטעי כמו לקדשי קדשים], אבל השתא דאמרת טעמא דריע חזקייהו ולא חיישינן דלמא אתי לאסוקי, כיון דלא אתי למטעי — מאי גדולה חזקה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:1:1.english: "And what, then, [is the meaning of] 'Great is presumptive status'?" - It is understandable if one does not elevate [to lineage]: [then] this [statement], "Great is presumptive status," is well-understood, even though there is [reason] to be concerned about an erring court that might elevate [them] from lifting of hands to [partaking of] most sacred offerings [and even though without presumptive status one elevates to terumah on the basis of a single witness, and we are not concerned about an erring court lest they elevate [him] to lineage — at this point the questioner thinks that lineage is more stringent, and they would not come to err [with it] as [they would] with most sacred offerings]; but now that you have said [that] the reason is that their presumptive status was undermined, and we are not concerned lest they come to elevate [them] — since they will not come to err, what [is the meaning of] "Great is presumptive status"?

Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:2:1.hebrew: וכי מסקינן מתרומה ליוחסין ה"מ בדאורייתא כו' - רבינו יצחק בן רבינו מאיר לא גריס לה, דהא "איבעית אימא" רב נחמן קאמר לה; ואי גרסי' לה, א"כ היה סותר בעצמו ראיה שהביא, דאי לא תימא הכי, למ"ד מעלין מתרומה ליוחסין הא אתי לאסוקי, אלא טעמא משום דריע חזקייהו. ואין זו סוגיית הש"ס אם לא יאמר "ולאו מילתא היא דאמרי". ובפ' עשרה יוחסין (קדושין סט:) גרסינן לה, ואגב שיטפא דהתם שיבשו לכותבה כאן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:2:1.english: "And when we elevate from teruma to lineage, this applies only to [teruma] by Torah [law], etc." - Rabbeinu Yitzchak ben Rabbeinu Meir does not have this reading, for Rav Nachman is the one who states [the answer of] "And if you wish, say"; and if we had this reading, then he himself would be contradicting the proof that he brought [earlier] — for if you do not say so, according to the one who holds that we elevate from teruma to lineage, it would come to elevating [them], [and] rather, the reason [they were not elevated] is because their presumptive status was weakened. And this is not the [usual] style of a Talmudic passage unless he says, "What I said is nothing [i.e., I retract]." And in the chapter [entitled] Asara Yuchasin (Kiddushin 69b) we have this reading, and due to the flow of [the passage] there, they mistakenly wrote it here.

Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:4:1.hebrew: לא במידי דאיקרי קדש - וא"ת: תרומה נמי איקרי קדשים, דכתיב: "ובא השמש וטהר ואחר יאכל מן הקדשים", וההוא קרא איירי בתרומה, דהעריב שמשו אוכל בתרומה? וי"ל: דודאי גבי טמא תרומה מיקרי קדשים, אבל הכא אאכילת זר קאמר, דלא אשכחן קדשים גבי אכילת זר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:4:1.english: Neither of items called kodesh - And if you ask: Terumah is also called kodashim, as it is written: "And when the sun sets he shall be pure, and afterward he may eat of the kodashim," and that verse refers to terumah, for one whose sun has set [after immersion] may eat terumah? One can answer: Certainly with respect to an impure person, terumah is called kodashim; however, here [the Gemara] is speaking of consumption by a non-priest, for we do not find [the term] kodashim [used for terumah] regarding consumption by a non-priest.

Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:5:1.hebrew: נשיאות כפים בבבל - דוקא נשיאות כפים, ולא אכילת חלה. ואע"ג דבסוריא נמי הוי מדרבנן — אין מדקדקין בבבל כמו בסוריא, דסבר האי תנא כיבוש יחיד שמיה כיבוש. ואכילת חלה בסוריא — ה"ה נשיאות כפים, כדמוכח לקמן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:5:1.english: The lifting of hands in Babylonia - Specifically the lifting of hands, and not eating ḥallah. And even though in Syria [ḥallah] is also by rabbinic decree — they are not as particular in Babylonia as in Syria, for this tanna holds [that] an individual conquest is considered a conquest. And [with regard to] eating ḥallah in Syria — the same applies to the lifting of hands, as is proven below.

Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:9:1.hebrew: לא חילוק גרנות גופה לחלה וקסבר תרומה כו' - וצ"ל דפליגי הנך ברייתות בפלוגתא דרב הונא בריה דרב יהושע ורבנן, דאי לאו הכי, בחד מהנך ברייתות ממה נפשך איכא למידק דמעלין מנשיאות כפים ליוחסין. ופליגי נמי, דלברייתא קמייתא אכילת חלה בסוריא חזקה לתרומה — וכל שכן דאכילת תרומה דאורייתא דהויא חזקה לאכילת חלה דרבנן; ובברייתא שניה קתני דחילוק גרנות, דהיינו תרומה, בסוריא לא הויא חזקה לחלה:
Tosafot on Ketubot 25a:9:1.english: "No, distribution at the threshing floors itself is for challah, and he holds that terumah, etc." - And we must say that these baraitot disagree in the dispute between Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua and the Rabbis, for if not so, either way, from one of these baraitot one could infer that we elevate from lifting of the hands to lineage. And they also disagree [in this]: according to the first baraita, eating challah in Syria is a presumptive status for terumah — and all the more so that eating terumah [which is] by Torah law is a presumptive status for eating challah [which is] by rabbinic law; whereas in the second baraita it teaches that distribution at the threshing floors, which is terumah, in Syria is not a presumptive status for challah.
